generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: WHERE AGENTS MEET THE BROWSER: BUILDING A BROWSER-NATIVE AGENT
Summary: LinkedIn built an internal AI agent that works across tools in employees' existing Chrome sessions, turning incident threads into tickets and documents into slide decks. It uses structured page data to cut token usage and tool-specific playbooks to improve reliability, while showing its actions and linking to evidence so users can verify the work.

Editorial idea:
AI agents are moving from isolated prompts into the user's active work environment, where visible actions and linked evidence determine whether automation can be trusted.

Central subject:
A browser-native AI agent carrying out multi-step workplace tasks inside an existing browser session.

Visual relationship:
The agent operates across browser tools while preserving a visible trail of actions and evidence for the employee to verify.

Composition:
Show one continuous browser workspace as a sequence of connected work areas: an incident discussion becoming a ticket and then a presentation, with the agent's path represented by physical handoffs between those areas and evidence attached at each step.

Permitted literal elements:
An incident discussion
A ticket document
A presentation document
Structured page content
Visible action records
Linked evidence connecting the outputs to their sources

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
Decorative racks
Standalone computer chips
Generic laptops unrelated to the browser workflow
Robots
Cloud imagery
Arrows without a grounded handoff
Logos
Rendered text
Unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Depicting the agent as an autonomous humanoid rather than software working inside a browser session
Showing isolated browser screens without the connected workflow
Suggesting unverified automation by omitting visible actions or evidence
Using generic AI imagery instead of the incident-to-ticket-to-presentation relationship

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
